title: What If Nobody Ever Wasted Food?

scenes.text: What if nobody wasted food? The numbers behind it are bigger than you'd guess.
About a third of all the food made in the world is never eaten.
Roughly thirteen percent is lost on the way to the store. Another nineteen percent is thrown away in homes, shops and restaurants.
All that rotting food adds up to eight to ten percent of the world's greenhouse gas emissions.
Meanwhile, up to seven hundred eighty-three million people go hungry.
So if the waste stopped, emissions would drop, and there'd be enough food already grown. The shortage isn't in the fields. It's in the trash.
